messages:
alex: heads up — spotted a billing mismatch when we compact traces across the 30s merge window for inference sidecars. customer on dedicated+private saw double-counting for a subset of requests.
maria: ugh, double-counting how? is that from duplicate envelopes or attribution shifting during late-enrich?
alex: looks like duplicates + late-enrich. flow: edge emits mini-envelopes without billing_key, ingest later enrich attaches billing_key, then the compact/merge pass dedups but attribution ends up applied twice in cost pipeline.
maria: can you paste a minimal example of the envelope sequence?
alex: sure

```# simplified
1) edge -> envelope(id=R1, billing_key=null, ts=100)
2) enrich job -> attach billing_key=B42 to id=R1, ts=115
3) merge window sees both raw and enriched envelope, merges to single trace but our cost-step counted both before merge finished
```

samir: so cost counting runs earlier than final dedupe? that matches the ingest ordering we implemented to keep latency low.
kevin: options: 1) move cost attribution after merge (accurate but could add tail latency), 2) attach provisional billing_key earlier (emit from edge), 3) gate-cost-with-merge-marker (mark an envelope as "final"), 4) late reconciliation job to correct counts.
maria: tradeoffs — #1 simplest correctness but might violate SLOs for sync reports. #2 requires SDK/sidecar changes and customers might not want to emit keys client-side for privacy. #3 needs upstream protocol change (merge marker) but keeps latency. #4 is complex and increases billing pipeline state.
alex: I prototyped a hybrid: keep attribution in the fast path but make it "merge-aware": when we attribute we emit a dedupe-hint (trace_fingerprint + candidate_id). If final merge later marks an envelope as canonical, the billing reconciler consumes hints and suppresses earlier attributions if duplicate.
samir: is that doable without storing full objects? we can use a compact bloom or TTLed KV entry keyed by fingerprint.
kevin: bloom will cause false positives (undercharge risk). TTLed KV per fingerprint (set on first attribution, cleared on canonical write) is safer but adds storage ops.
maria: storage ops at attribution time -> cost. but we could batch KV writes and rely on async best-effort; we already accept small reconciliation windows for export metrics.
alex: proposed plan:
- implement fingerprint (sha256 of request_id + route) at edge
- on attribution write KV:key=fingerprint value=attribution_id TTL=2m
- merge step writes canonical=fingerprint with canonical_id
- reconciliation reads KV and marks duplicates for reversal (async job). fallback: if KV missing, run late-enrich lookup as existing logic.

kevin: rollout plan?
alex: feature-flagged rollout: enable on internal tenant -> canary on us-east-dedicated -> 48h metrics check (billing delta, SLOs) -> opt-in for customers. Also add telemetry: KV latency, reconciliation rate, false-reconcile count.
samir: metric to watch: ratio of initial attributions reversed by reconciliation. aim <0.1% on canary.
maria: docs: update instrumentation guide to show fingerprinting and privacy note (don't include PII). also ensure KMS keys not leaked by fingerprints.
ops-bot: deploy triggered: eng-platform/release/obs-dedupe-hint v0.1 -> canary queue
kevin: open question: what TTL for KV? 2m seems OK given merge window is 30s but allow network jitter. maybe 5m to be safe.
alex: ok will adjust to 5m in prototype. i'll create RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and perf numbers. assigning tasks: alex -> implement KV hint + reconciler prototype; samir -> cost-pipeline changes to accept dedupe-suppress marker; kevin -> rollout/telemetry; maria -> docs + privacy blurb.
maria: thanks, ping when prototype PR is ready, i can review the privacy text.
alex: will do. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks team.
